body:
A tested correction, for anyone training on these segments before the data is regenerated. Sampling the CT at tifxyz cell (y + dy, x + dx), with dy and dx from the per-segment fits in the repo README, lines HF65 slice 32 up with the CT to within 0.4 px on both axes in all 32 regions I ran: the 24 the fits came from and 8 they never saw (two new regions per Paris4 segment, one on w018, and the held-out w01 region). Before the correction the same regions were off by up to 254 px on one axis, and afterwards the NCC peak sits at zero shift in every region.

![w01_r15, a region the fit never saw: checkerboard of HF65 slice 32 and the CT on the tifxyz, before (left) and after (right)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/a7b7468/png/w01_before_after.png)

`correct/apply_fit.py` in https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment maps canvas pixels to tifxyz cells and back and resamples a canvas or label tile into the tifxyz frame, which is the grid `full_3d` reads. The before/after table for every region is in `correct/RESULTS.md`. It covers only the four measured segments and still assumes the labels sit on the canvas pixels. Storing the transform in the segment metadata, or rendering the canvas from the tifxyz beside it, would fix this at the source.

I ran the same measurement on the rest of the training segments in `ink/`, which answers most of the "not checked" line above. Of the 32 segment folders the shipped `full_3d` configs read (`dino_guided_teacher` lists all eight scroll dirs; the Paris4 ones are also in `dino_guided_v1`/`v2`/`v3`), 26 have a canvas that does not line up with its tifxyz (24 measured now, plus w01 and w05 from above), 5 line up, and 1 I could not measure. By scroll: every Paris4, 1667 and 0139 training segment is off, and so is the 0009b one. 0500p2, the three 841 segments and MAN5 line up.

**The w018 one-cell shift is on eleven more segments.** 1667 w013, w023, w028, w029 and w031, 0009b `auto_grown_20250919055754487_inp_hr_2um`, and 0139 w016, w017, w028, w029 and w030 all show a constant (-19.6, -19.6) level-0 px, the same value as w018. That is one stored cell at tifxyz scale 0.05 (20 px) minus the renderer's +0.35. On these folders the tifxyz, canvas and label sizes are identical, so the metadata gives no hint and `validate_segments.py` passes them. Where I measured regions far apart (w013, 0009b, w016) they agree within 0.1 px.

**0139 w035, w039, w040, w041, w043 and w044 have a different constant shift, (+30.7, -49.3) px.** I don't know where it comes from, but on w040 it is the bucket canvas that is off. The S3 render `PHerc0139/segments/20250831000000-w040_2025083102/surface-volumes/2.399um-0.22m-78keV-volume-20260102150214.zarr` has the same size as the bucket canvas and lines up with the CT at the tifxyz cells to within 0.6 px. The tifxyz in the bucket folder is the S3 mesh on 20260102150214 (same bbox, same x.tif values), so it is not a mesh from another scan.

**The other Paris4 segments drift like w00 and w05.** w02, w03, w06, w07 and w09 each have a full-resolution tifxyz size that differs from the canvas by 23 to 54 px per axis. Two regions per segment fit d = a + (full/canvas - 1) x position with a constant intercept of about (-21, +12) px at tifxyz scale 0.1, and (-42, +23) on w07 at scale 0.05, which matches the w05 fit above. Extrapolated to the segment corners the offset reaches 42 px on one axis (w07); the largest I measured directly is 35.5 px.

**Aligned**, at the expected +0.35 px: 0500p2 `-1`, 841 `w00`, `auto_grown_20260220144552896` and `auto_grown_20260220174252405`, and MAN5_outer_3 (its canvas is fine; #2369 is about its label zarrs). These also show that the method does not add a shift of its own.

**Not measured:** `814_46527_2um_try2`. Its canvas was rendered from a 2.403 um scan that is not in the open data bucket, and the 2.4 um volume that is there (20251130) is a different scan.

Method, per region: sample the CT at the tifxyz cells on the canvas lattice, then find the shift that best matches high-passed slice 32 of the canvas (masked NCC over a ±128 px window, sub-pixel peak fit). A second implementation written separately (phase correlation on gradient magnitude, with its own tifxyz and CT sampling) agrees within 0.4 px on w013, w035, w040 and Paris4 w07, including regions the first one never used, and gives +0.2 to +0.4 px on the 0500p2 and MAN5 controls. Scripts, the per-segment table, per-region results and overlay images for one segment per group are in [`audit/`](https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/tree/main/audit) of the same repo. A rerun fetches only byte ranges from the public buckets (about 1.1 GB for all regions).

Some follow-up, starting with prior art I should have found before opening this.

**`tifxyz_label_transfer` already handles a constant canvas offset.** `vesuvius/src/vesuvius/tifxyz_label_transfer` (added in #1943 on 2026-10-01) notes that annotations drawn on published renders "do not always sit pixel-for-pixel on the TIFXYZ canvas". Its QA workflow measures the offset from CT and applies it through `--label-canvas-offset DY DX`, with pherc0139-w039 as the example, and `docs/theory.md` uses the same sign as this issue. So the 0139 shift was known. What this issue adds is the training side: the ink_detection `full_3d` loader reads the bucket labels against the tifxyz with no offset, on 26 segments. The one-cell group is constant too, so that flag could carry it, but the Paris4 offsets are linear in position and one constant does not cover them.

**The 0139 shift is the integer (+30, -50).** On w040 two direct measurements give it. The bucket canvas against the S3 render of the same mesh peaks at (+30.002, -49.991) at level 0 (NCC 0.994), and the S3 `ink-labels/2.399um-volume-20260102150214/20260918/` w040 inklabels and supervision are the bucket ones moved by exactly (30, -50), with intersection equal to union. My (+30.7, -49.3) above is the same offset read through the CT registration, which also reads +0.4 to +0.5 on the aligned segments. It comes from two parts:

- (+30, +30). The canvases match a render of the coarse `tifxyz_normalized` mesh at 80 px per coarse cell, and the shipped tifxyz is a 4x resample of that mesh with fine index f = 4c + 1.5. Each surface point lands 1.5 fine cells (30 px at scale 0.05) later on both axes. With resample factor u and scale s this is (u - 1) / (2s), so the metadata predicts it.
- (0, -80), one more coarse cell along x only. My best guess is that the render used a column-mirrored copy of the mesh and the image was mirrored back, because in this renderer a vertex mirror and an image mirror differ by one cell. A mesh sitting one column over gives identical pixels, so the data cannot separate the two, and no metadata field records either.

w041 and w044 cannot be checked against S3 this way: their S3 meshes differ from the bucket ones (w044 by a rotation of about 1 degree), so for them (+30, -50) rests on the CT registration alone. If these canvases get re-rendered, resampling the tifxyz with srcX = dstX / u avoids the (u - 1) / (2s) term, and re-rendering after a mesh flip avoids the extra cell. A validator step that renders one 512 px level-0 patch from the shipped tifxyz and cross-correlates it with the canvas would show these shifts; on w040 one patch gave the offset to 0.01 px, while `validate_segments.py` passes the one-cell folders because their sizes match.

**Shift file for the 26 segments.** [`correct/shifts/`](https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/tree/main/correct/shifts) has one row per offset segment, with conventions in `shifts.json` and `apply_shifts.py` to map points and resample label tiles. I checked every row on a region it was not fitted to, with the same registration. Before correction those regions are off by 6.6 to 147 px; after it the largest residual on either axis is 0.55 px (Paris4 w06), and the NCC peak goes up on every one. The five aligned segments go through the identity map unchanged. Given the +0.4 to +0.5 the method reads on aligned segments and the 0.7 px gap to the exact w040 value, I'd treat the rows as good to about 1 px, a quarter of a level-2 voxel. The constant rows can go straight into `--label-canvas-offset`.

Which fix do you want for training? One option is for the loader to read a per-segment shift table like this one. The other is to regenerate the bucket canvases and labels on the tifxyz grid, which the S3 `20260918` labels already do for w040. I can open a PR for the loader route if that is the direction, but I'd rather not guess.

I ran a GPU test of what the offset costs training, in case it helps with the question above. I trained villa's `full_3d` ink trainer (37d1897fb, 12,000 steps) on PHercParis4 w00 and 1667 w018 with corrected labels, the labels as shipped, and corrected labels moved 32, 64 or 128 px in y, then scored every run on held-out boxes against corrected labels. Segment w018 did not learn and the pre-registered gate (pooled AUC 0.70) failed, so the comparison is exploratory and covers w00 only, where the models reach about 0.74 AUC.

On w00, training on the labels as shipped or moved 32 or 64 px gave no detectable drop in held-out AUC. Moved 128 px, the labels cost 0.051 AUC (95% interval 0.025 to 0.077, four seeds each). Moving only the held-out labels cost more: 0.026 to 0.029 AUC at 64 px and about 0.08 at 128 px. So at this scale the offsets matter most for validation and scoring, and in training once they reach about 128 px. The rules for each step were frozen before the runs they read, and everything reruns from [`labelshift/`](https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/tree/main/labelshift).

A stronger model may be more sensitive to the offset, so I also scored, without a GPU, an idealized model that copies the moved labels exactly. At 64 px it loses 21% of its margin over chance, a bit above the 17% the runs rule out, and blurring its output by half a training voxel or more brings it under that. The trained models' costs sit close to the same model blurred by 2 to 4 voxels. Details are in the README's [Ceiling check](https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/tree/main/labelshift#ceiling-check) section.

Update with a pre-registered training test on Paris4 w01, the segment with the largest offset I measured (up to 288 px over its supervised area). On w01 the shipped labels do cost training.

I trained villa's `full_3d` ink trainer (37d1897fb, 12,000 steps, `volume_scale` 2) on w01 alone: four seeds on the labels as shipped, and four on the same labels resampled into the tifxyz frame with the w01 fit. Every run was scored on three held-out boxes against the corrected labels. Mean held-out AUC was 0.837 with the corrected labels and 0.743 with the labels as shipped, a difference of 0.094 (95% interval 0.064 to 0.123). Every corrected-label run scored above every as-shipped run. Scored against the shipped labels inside the boxes instead, the corrected-label models were still ahead (0.632 against 0.599).

The decision rule was frozen in the repo before the first run (commit e8b832b). What happened after that, a rerun after an S3 outage and a machine restart between runs, is in `DEVIATIONS.md`. The table, per-run configs and evaluations are in [`labelshift-w01/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/stantheman0128/vesuvius-hf65-alignment/blob/main/labelshift-w01/RESULTS.md). It is one segment trained on its own and scored on three areas of it.

On the fix: `tifxyz_label_transfer/estimate_canvas_offset.py` already fits translation plus linear drift, but `--label-canvas-offset` in `transfer.py` takes a constant offset, and w01's offset is mostly drift. I can add the drift term there in a PR if that is the route you want, or leave it if the bucket labels are going to be regenerated.
